front.title: Binding Decisions and Settlements to Agent Action Records

abstract.t:
This document extends [I-D.psi-agent-01], which records what a software agent did. A record of an action does not show who said the work was to be done, what the model asked to do, what a policy engine permitted, or what was paid.
This document defines four statements -- a mandate, a proposal, a decision, and a settlement -- and the rules that bind them to a chain of action records under one run identifier. Each statement is signed by its own party with its own key. A verifier that holds the statements can test, offline and without trusting the agent, whether the action chain is unbroken, whether the decision that permitted it was signed by a key other than the one named as the acting key, and whether the amount settled lay inside the limit the mandate declared.
A valid envelope shows that identified parties made these statements and that the statements have not changed since they were sealed. It does not show that any statement was correct, sufficient, lawful, or true, and it makes no legal representation of any kind.
